texts: Why does Old Vesh tell the story of the bad winter of sixty-three years ago?

fields.sentence: Why does Old Vesh tell the story of the bad winter of sixty-three years ago?
parse: (: $prf (And (Name $v "Old Vesh") (Member $e tell) (Agent $e $v) (Theme $e $s) (Member $s story) (Of $s $w) (Member $w winter) (Member $w bad) (BeforeBy $w now 63 year) (ReasonFor $r $e)) $tv)

q2_gaps: aboutness "of"-phrase on a non-deverbal noun ("the story of the bad winter"): the genitive rule explicitly excludes an about-phrase from Possession, and "story" is neither a nominalization whose verb takes the of-NP as object nor a true relational noun, so no head is assigned to it — the parse's entity-attached (Of $s $w) is an extension by analogy with the nominalization oblique
review.notes: The "why" query is one line with (ReasonFor $r $e) on a correctly built focus pattern, the name bound by its full surface string, no status atom for the present habitual, "bad" kept as a separate descriptive property, and "sixty-three years ago" rendered as (BeforeBy $w now 63 year) on the event-denoting winter noun.
